long_run_roe.why: Nonprime consumer lending is competitive and cyclical, and funding costs are rising. The 2021-2025 record fell from 38% to 16-25%, so a fade to about 16% is above the 9.3% cost of equity but well below recent levels. The new bank charter could cut funding costs, but it is unquantified and not yet open.

roe.why: Nine-month 2026 net income is $563m, down from $579m, and Q3 pretax fell on a higher provision. Adding a Q4 near $190m gives about $750m on $3,401m opening equity, or about 22%, below the 24.5% of 2025. Years 2-5 ease slightly as funding costs and normalising credit weigh, while growth and operating leverage partly offset.

terminal_growth.why: Long-run book growth is set a little below the nominal anchor of 3.75%, because a mature consumer lender in a competitive, regulated market grows with receivables and nominal income.

risks.risk: Credit deterioration in the nonprime book (unemployment rise) lifts charge-offs and provisions, cutting earnings.
Funding squeeze or loss of capital-market access forces slower growth, with fixed-rate loans that cannot be repriced against rising cost of funds.
Management keeps buybacks high and leverage rises, so book equity stays flat.

situation.roe_position: ROE is high because common book equity is small (about $3.4bn) against $26.3bn of receivables, so a 22.6% yield on nonprime loans less funding and loss costs lands on a thin equity base. 2025 ROE of 24.5% was lifted by lower charge-offs than 2024 (2024 ROE was 16.0%). In 2026 the provision is rising with growth and a higher charge-off ratio (Q3 provision $615m vs $488m), and funding cost is up, so ROE is drifting down to about 22%. No large one-offs are visible, apart from debt-repurchase losses that are now small.
situation.why: OMF is a non-bank lender with no parent-level regulatory capital ratio in the packet, but net leverage of 5.5x adjusted capital and debt covenants limit how far equity can lag receivables growth. Dividends of about $4.20 a share plus buybacks absorb nearly all earnings, so book equity was flat in 2026 (3,401 to 3,391). Growth of 7-9% in receivables will probably require a slower buyback pace or retention of more earnings, which would lift book growth a little. The packet does not show covenant headroom or debt maturities.

book_growth.why: Equity was flat over nine months as buybacks of 173 and dividends of 371 absorbed most of the 563 of earnings. Receivables are growing about 7-9%, which at constant leverage needs some equity growth, so growth should rise to about 3-4% after 2026.

fade_years.why: The above-cost-of-equity return reflects an established branch, digital and dealer franchise with scale in nonprime credit, so it should erode only slowly. The OneMain Bank charter, which is still conditional and about a year from opening, adds uncertainty to that fade rather than shortening it.

situation.base_year_representative_note: 2025 was above the 2024 trough and the 2026 run-rate is lower.
situation.roe_position: Return on equity of 0.2454 in 2025 is high for a lender with 5.5x net leverage. It was lifted by a 2025 rebound from the 2024 trough of 0.1598, when provisions and Foursight-related items weighed. In 2026 the provision is rising faster than interest income because the allowance is built up front on fast receivables growth. Nine-month net income was 563 against 579 a year earlier, so the 2026 return should drift down to about 0.22. Funding costs are also rising, and charge-offs are still elevated.
situation.why: Book equity is roughly flat (3,391 at September 2026 against 3,401 at December 2025) because dividends and buybacks absorb most of earnings. The business is funded with debt at 5.5x net leverage and grows receivables about 7-9% a year, so equity growth is limited by leverage and by the payout policy. This is a non-bank lender; the covenants and funding markets set the limit rather than a bank capital ratio. Equity growth should therefore be modest, about 0.5% in 2026 and 3-4% a year afterwards.

quotes: Our operations are subject to regular examination by state regulators and U.S. federal and foreign regulators.

risks.basis: Stated in the 8-K. The delay risk is inferred from the conditions.
risks.claim: The newly approved OneMain Bank industrial-bank charter is still conditional and not yet operating: it opens in about one year and must complete its organization plan and meet regulatory requirements first.
quotes: OneMain Bank will be required to complete its organization plan and satisfy applicable regulatory requirements before opening for business.

unresolved_questions.basis: stated in P7 for the driver; the missing split is inferred from the absence of an allowance roll-forward in the packet
unresolved_questions.claim: The Q3 provision was $615 million against $488 million a year earlier, and management attributes the $146 million allowance increase to receivables growth. It is not clear how much of the provision rise comes from growth and how much from a weaker loss outlook or changed macro assumptions.
quotes: During the third quarter of 2026, the allowance for finance receivable losses increased $146 million driven by receivables growth.

unresolved_questions.basis: inferred from the quarterly ratios in P7; no seasonality analysis is in the packet
unresolved_questions.claim: The consumer loan net charge-off ratio fell to 6.89% in Q3 from 7.77% in Q2, but it is above the 6.67% of Q3 2025. It is unclear whether the Q3 drop is seasonal or a lasting improvement in credit.

unresolved_questions.basis: inferred from receivable balances in P7 and the year-end card delinquency data in P3; Q3 2026 card credit metrics are not in the packet
unresolved_questions.claim: Credit card receivables grew to $1,383 million from $834 million a year earlier (table in millions). The 10-K showed higher delinquency and allowance ratios for cards than for consumer loans, and the packet does not show how newer card cohorts are performing.

unresolved_questions.basis: inferred from F3 and the leverage table in P7; no remaining authorization or forward plan is stated in the packet
unresolved_questions.claim: Share repurchases were 173 (table in millions) in the nine months against 70 a year earlier, while net leverage was 5.5x and receivables kept growing. The evidence does not say how much of the $1.0 billion authorization remains or whether the pace of capital return will continue.

unresolved_questions.basis: stated in P7 for the balances; the missing maturity detail is inferred from the omitted MD&A text
unresolved_questions.claim: Principal debt was $24.4 billion, 52% of it secured. The packet does not show the maturity schedule, covenant headroom or refinancing needs.
quotes: As of September 30, 2026, the Company had principal debt balances outstanding of $24.4 billion, 52% of which was secured.

unresolved_questions.basis: inferred from the note reference in F1; the note text is not in the packet
unresolved_questions.claim: The balance sheet carries a Contingencies note (Note 12), but the packet does not include its content. It cannot be determined whether any legal or regulatory matter is material.
quotes: Contingencies (Note 12)

unresolved_questions.basis: stated in P8 for the approval and conditions; economic effects are inferred as unknown from the absence of figures
unresolved_questions.claim: OneMain Bank received approval subject to customary conditions and must still complete its organization plan. The evidence does not show the effect on funding cost, capital, expenses or the company's non-bank status.
quotes: OneMain Bank will be required to complete its organization plan and satisfy applicable regulatory requirements before opening for business.

verdict_reason: expected return +10.6 points a year against the required return over 3 years
